title: DP-S4S: Accurate and Scalable Select-Join-Aggregate Query Processing with User-Level Differential Privacy

statements.text: For $ >0$ and $δ≥ 0$, a randomized mechanism $ : I O $ is $( ,δ)$-DP, if for any pair of neighboring database instances $ I ~ I '$ and any subset of outputs $O O $, it holds that \[ [ ( I ) O]≤ e^ · [ ( I ') O]+δ\,. \] When $δ=0$, we say the mechanism satisfies pure DP . Otherwise (i.e., when $δ>0$), we say the mechanism satisifes approximate DP . Note that in the above definition, the concept of ``neighboring'' database instances $ I ~ I '$ is left abstract, which we will clarify with concrete definitions in Section~ [ref] . A common approach to answering numerical queries under differential privacy is to inject random noise into the query results, whose scale is calibrated to the sensitivity of the query. The widely used notion of global sensitivity ( GS ) considers all possible neighboring instances in the domain $ I $, as follows. [Global Sensitivity~ [cite] ] Given $F: I R ^d$, the global sensitivity of $F$ is defined as \[ _F:=max_ I , I ' I : I ~ I ' \|F( I )-F( I ')\|\,. \]
